# Welcome!

I am [Vinícius Fonsêca dos Santos]{.underline}, a Ph.D. candidate in the [Graduate Program in Entomology](https://www.pos.entomologia.ufv.br/) at the [Universidade Federal de Viçosa](https://www.ufv.br/campus-vicosa/) (UFV), Brazil. I hold a B.Sc. in Agronomy from the [Universidade Federal do Espírito Santo](https://www.ufes.br/) (UFES) and an M.Sc. in Entomology (2023) from UFV.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## About This Website

This website serves as an open science and reproducible digital notebook hosting the **statistical analyses and data visualizations for my Ph.D. thesis**. Built using Quarto and R, it organizes experimental workflows, statistical models, and graphical outputs in a structured and transparent format.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Research Overview

My doctoral research investigates the **suppression of collective defenses and social immunity in leaf-cutting ants (*Atta sexdens*) when exposed to modulating plant substrates**.

Leaf-cutting ants are major agricultural and forestry pests in the Neotropics. Their ecological success and resilience against pest management strategies rely heavily on complex eusocial mechanisms—such as **social immunity** (grooming and pathogen decontamination) and **strict substrate selection** to protect their symbiotic fungus. However, certain botanical substrates, such as garden nasturtium (*Tropaeolum majus*), can bypass these defensive barriers and disrupt colony homeostasis.

Key objectives of my thesis include: **Social Immunity & Collective Defenses:** Evaluating how continuous exposure to *T. majus* alters grooming behaviors, pathogen decontamination (*Metarhizium anisopliae*), and social network dynamics among nestmates. **Bait Dissemination & Caste Interactions:** Analyzing how inter-caste interaction networks and the internal flow of toxic bait (*isocicloseram*) are modified following plant substrate exposure. **Substrate Selection & Risk Perception:** Assessing whether exposed colonies lose their capacity to discriminate and reject unsuitable, toxic, or pathogen-contaminated plant materials.

Feel free to explore the statistical code and visualizations! If you have any questions, suggestions, or ideas for scientific collaboration, please feel free to reach out.
